title: Pre-conditional Voluntary General Offer by Allianz for Income Insurance
what_it_is: Pre-conditional Voluntary General Offer by Allianz for Income Insurance

sections.label: Allianz Income transaction decision
sections.summary: NE committed to sell Income shares for Allianz to acquire a majority stake; the Government decided the transaction should not proceed in its current form.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As part of the proposed transaction, NTUC Enterprise, or NE, had given a legal commitment to sell a proportion of its shares in Income to enable Allianz to acquire a majority stake in Income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The Government has assessed the proposed transaction and has decided that it would not be in the public interest for the transaction, in its current form, to proceed.

sections.label: NE Income shareholding and injection
sections.summary: NE is a co-op holding about 72% of Income shares and injected $630 million into Income between 2015 and 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: NE is also a co-op and currently holds about 72% of the shares in Income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: NE injected a total of $630 million into Income between 2015 and 2020.

sections.label: Income customer numbers
sections.summary: As of 31 December 2023, Income Insurance covered close to 1.7 million customers, aiming to serve one in two Singaporeans by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As of 31 December 2023, Income Insurance covered close to 1.7 million customers, with an ambition to serve one in two Singaporeans by 2025.

sections.label: Income EGM corporatisation vote
sections.summary: At the EGM on 18 February 2022, Income's members voted overwhelmingly in support of corporatisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: At the EGM on 18 February 2022, Income's members voted overwhelmingly in support of corporatisation.

sections.label: Income corporatisation exemption and completion
sections.summary: Income sought and was granted an exemption from section 88 of the CSA, carried over about S$2 billion surplus, and completed corporatisation on 6 April 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Income thus sought an exemption from section 88 of the CSA as part of the corporatisation, which I granted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Following this exemption, Income carried over approximately S$2 billion in surplus to the new corporate entity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The corporatisation exercise was completed on 6 April 2023.

sections.label: Income low-cost schemes and contribution
sections.summary: Income will maintain two low-cost insurance schemes and contribute $100 million over 10 years from 2021 for social and environmental causes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, Income will maintain two low-cost insurance schemes as well as contribute $100 million over 10 years from 2021 for social and environmental causes.

sections.label: Allianz projects Income cash return
sections.summary: Allianz projects Income would return about S$1.85 billion in cash to shareholders within three years after completion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Allianz projects that Income would return some S$1.85 billion in cash to its shareholders, within the first three years after completion of the transaction.

sections.label: Government intervention after MCCY review
sections.summary: After MCCY reviewed the proposed transaction, the Government found sufficient basis to intervene to protect the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It was at this point, after MCCY reviewed the information on the proposed transaction, that we became concerned.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We decided that there was sufficient basis for the Government to intervene in the proposed transaction to protect the public interest, notwithstanding that the financial prudential requirements had been satisfied.

sections.label: Income surplus exemption to new entity
sections.summary: Income obtained an exemption to carry over a S$2 billion surplus to the new entity instead of the CSLA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As I had explained, as part of that exercise, Income had sought and obtained an exemption to allow it to carry over a surplus of S$2 billion to the new corporate entity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: If not for the Ministerial exemption in 2023, Income co-op's accumulated surplus of some S$2 billion would have gone to the CSLA after being wound up, to benefit the co-op movement in Singapore as a whole.

sections.label: Cumulative risk to public interest
sections.summary: MCCY judges the capital extraction and lack of structural protections cumulatively unacceptable, so the transaction is not in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On their own, these factors would not have caused MCCY to object to the transaction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: However, taken together with the proposed capital extraction and the lack of structural protections in the deal to ensure the continuation of Income's social mission, cumulatively, they pose a risk that MCCY judges not to be acceptable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As such, it is the Government's view that it is not in the public interest for the transaction, in its current form, to proceed.

sections.label: Open to new arrangements
sections.summary: The Government will not allow the transaction but is open to new arrangements if the concerns are fully addressed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Whilst we will not allow the proposed transaction to proceed, we are nonetheless open to any new arrangement which Income may wish to pursue, whether with Allianz or any other partners, so long as the concerns highlighted are fully addressed.

sections.label: Amending Insurance Act for MCCY views
sections.summary: The Government intends to amend the Insurance Act to give a statutory basis for MCCY's views in such approvals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: There is currently no provision in the Insurance Act for MAS to consider the views of MCCY, in the case of an application relating to an insurer that is either a co-op or linked to a co-op.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We therefore intend to amend the Insurance Act to provide a clear statutory basis for MCCY's views to be considered in any approval involving such applications.

sections.label: Insurance Act amendment Bill readings
sections.summary: Minister Chee Hong Tat will table the First Reading of an Insurance Act amendment Bill urgently, with Second and Third Readings proposed on 16 October 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Following this Ministerial Statement, Minister Chee Hong Tat will table the First Reading of an amendment Bill to the Insurance Act on an urgent basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Given the time sensitivity of this matter, the Second and Third Readings are proposed to be taken on Wednesday, 16 October 2024.

sections.label: NE shares converted to permanent shares
sections.summary: NE's 2015 undertaking not to redeem shares became irrelevant after the 2018 CSA amendment allowed permanent shares, which NE converted to, stabilising Income's capital base.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: NE's commitment not to redeem its shares was meant to assure Income of the stability of its capital base, pending legislative amendments to provide for a more permanent class of share capital for co-ops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The CSA was subsequently amended in 2018 to allow institutional members of co-ops, like NE, to hold permanent shares so that the capital could not be withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: NE then converted all its shares in Income to permanent shares, which could count towards MAS' capital adequacy requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This rendered NE's 2015 undertaking no longer relevant, because NE's shares were now legally locked in and Income's capital base had stabilised.

sections.label: Insurance Act amendment Bill tabling
sections.summary: The amendment Bill to the Insurance Act will be tabled after this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: As I said, the amendment Bill to the Insurance Act will be tabled after this.

sections.label: No financial reason to reject arrangement
sections.summary: The answer is no; on financial and prudential reasons there is no reason not to accept the arrangement, with grounds relating to representations, the exemption and proposed capital extraction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: As I have said in my speech, the answer is no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: On financial and prudential reasons alone, let me make clear, there is no reason not to accept this arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The grounds that I have set up relate to the representations that were made at the corporatisation exercise, the exemption that was granted and the circumstances in which now it is proposed for capital to be extracted.

sections.label: MAS unaware of MCCY considerations
sections.summary: MAS did not share regulatory information with other agencies and was unaware of MCCY's considerations when the section 88 exemption was issued, so it did not link Allianz's proposal to the exemption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The information received by MAS to perform its regulatory functions is generally not shared with other Government agencies and at that time, MAS was not aware of MCCY's considerations when MCCY issued the section 88 exemption and hence, it did not link the proposal from Allianz with the exemption that MCCY had provided earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As the MAS team were still doing their technical assessments at that time, they did not surface the details, including the capital reduction plan, to the MAS Board before the 6 August Parliament Sitting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: It was only after the 6 August Parliament Sitting that the MAS team that was assessing this matter saw that this plan to optimise the capital could be relevant to MCCY's views on the proposed transaction.

sections.label: Exemption and surplus funds transfer
sections.summary: When the exemption was granted, about S$2 billion of surplus funds was transferred into Income instead of the CSLA, and extracting it now runs counter to the exemption's premises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: For instance, Mr Liang would recall that I spent some time explaining the background to the corporatisation and the exemption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, going back to this specific case, when the exemption was granted, the surplus funds of about S$2 billion, instead of going to the CSLA which would have applied for the benefit of all co-ops in Singapore, was transferred into Income, the entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is how we saw it and that is why the exemption was given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But in the context of those representations – building up its surplus, share capital base and so on – to come forward now and to ask for it to be extracted so soon and at this amount, after the exercise was completed, in our view, runs counter to the premises on which the exemption was granted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is why in this case we have stepped in.

sections.label: Allianz rationale and MCCY intervention
sections.summary: MCCY learned of the transaction terms and planned capital remittance only after the 6 August Sitting, then decided to intervene.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: From what I can see from the announcements back in July, a key rationale that Allianz put forth was that it will undertake a strategic and operational review of the company to operate it in a more capital efficient manner, considering possible business model transformation opportunities and also to target a double digit return from investment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I had explained earlier that MCCY was not aware of the terms of the transaction or indeed of the planned cash remittance which includes the capital extraction until after the 6 August Parliamentary Sitting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It was at that juncture, and I think Minister Chee shared the circumstances in which MAS shared the information with MCCY, which I also covered in my Statement, and thereafter we decided to intervene, based on what we found out from the terms of the transaction as disclosed at the point in time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: And if so, will MCCY consider further mechanisms to be built in since subsequent corporate exercises could alter or weaken this social objective?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It essentially is competing with large players around the world and in Singapore and it also has to maintain a substantial capital base.

sections.label: Section 88 exemption if wound up
sections.summary: The exemption would not apply if Income were wound up and no longer continued its business, as section 88 would apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In terms of the exemption, as I had explained, if Income was going to be wound up and no longer continuing with its business, obviously, section 88 would apply.

sections.label: Possible CSA amendments for conversions
sections.summary: MCCY would look at possibly amending the CSA for scenarios where a co-operative converts into a corporate vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In terms of future steps that Mr Goh mentioned, I mentioned in my Statement that we would look at the possibility of amendments to the CSA to look at such scenarios where a co-operative converts into a corporate vehicle and what are some of the measures that can be taken.

sections.label: Income capital adequacy and MAS approval
sections.summary: Income has sufficient resources to meet its capital adequacy ratio, and MAS has not yet approved the proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Income has sufficient resources to meet the necessary capital adequacy ratio, which means it has enough capital to meet its liabilities and also to pay out to policy-holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I also want to add, Mr Deputy Speaker, that MAS has not yet approved this proposal.

sections.label: Bill for non-prudential considerations
sections.summary: The Insurance Act lacks explicit provision for non-prudential assessment, so the Bill gives the Minister-in-charge these powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The current provisions in the Insurance Act do not provide explicitly a provision for the Minister-in-charge of MAS, or for MAS to assess an application like this, based on non-prudential related considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, this is why we need to make this amendment through the proposed Bill to give the Minister-in-charge of MAS these powers, to be able to factor in non-prudential related considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: In this case, relating to co-ops and with views from the Minister for MCCY.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We want to make sure that when we regulate, we do so in an even-handed manner, in an open manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: And as Minister Tong mentioned earlier, and I would like to reiterate that, the reason why we have concerns about this particular deal is not because there is a foreign entity, Allianz in this case, and it is also not because we have concerns about Allianz being fit and proper and being a suitable partner for Income.

sections.label: MAS referred capital reduction to MCCY
sections.summary: After the 6 August Sitting, MAS recognised a larger consideration, passed information on the proposed capital reduction to MCCY.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, regardless of who the entity is, we would have to apply those rules based on our considerations as a prudential regulator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I also explained earlier in my response to Ms Pereira that after the 6 August Parliament Sitting, the team from MAS that was looking at this proposal then recognised that there is a larger consideration beyond just prudential considerations alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: They then passed this information to MCCY, the information about the proposed capital reduction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: MAS was the one who provided this information to MCCY and said, "I think this is something you need to take a look at and whether this will fit with the terms of the earlier exemption that MCCY provided".

sections.label: Government public interest decision
sections.summary: The Government collectively decided it would not serve the public interest to allow this to proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Collectively, we looked at it and came to a view, as a Government, on what would serve the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And, in this case, we decided that it would not serve the public interest to allow this to proceed.

sections.label: Factors tipping the balance
sections.summary: After 6 August, a substantial capital extraction after the 2023 exemption tipped the balance, prompting a review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Yes, you lose board majority and you lose shareholding majority, but you take that in the round and on balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But what we discovered after 6 August, with a substantial capital extraction, shortly after the exemption was granted in 2023, of such a substantial amount, were factors which then tipped the balance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And then we said, as I mentioned in my speech, cumulatively, these factors caused us to have pause and we decided to review it in greater detail, and we realised that this was not something that we should see through as a matter of public interest.

sections.label: Capital optimisation and capital adequacy
sections.summary: Capital optimisation may allow withdrawal without compromising sustainability, and MAS assessed capital adequacy over three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I am not saying that this is what happened in this case, but these are some reasons why you might have a capital optimisation which provides for withdrawal but still not compromise the longer-term financial sustainability of the entity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I think the Member heard me mention earlier that on MAS' assessment, even after the withdrawal, over a three-year period, the capital adequacy requirements of the new entity will still have to pass muster.

sections.label: MAS not approving capital reduction
sections.summary: Minister Chee added that MAS has not approved the proposed capital reduction plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Minister Chee Hong Tat, would you like to add to the response?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I just wanted to add to what Minister Tong has said in response to Ms He Ting Ru that MAS has not approved the proposed capital reduction plan.

sections.label: Allianz proposed capital reduction
sections.summary: The proposed capital reduction is a proposal from Allianz.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But in case Mr Leong may have missed it earlier, let me say that again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, first, I think we have to understand that the proposed capital reduction is a proposal from Allianz.

sections.label: Answer is yes
sections.summary: The answer must be yes because this is part of the proposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The answer must be yes, because this is part of the proposal.

sections.label: Capital adequacy ratio after extraction
sections.summary: Minister Tong and the speaker explained that capital adequacy ratios could still be met after the extraction, and MAS will assess this independently as regulator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Earlier, when we were discussing this matter of capital adequacy ratio, I think Minister Tong and I were explaining that because of the way the capital was being optimised in the proposal, the capital adequacy ratios, even after the extraction, could still be met.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: MAS will of course have to assess this independently as regulator to see if we agree with that view.

sections.label: Government concerns over Allianz deal
sections.summary: Minister Tong explained the Government's concerns, while NE and NTUC intended the Allianz deal to strengthen Income, which is why the matter comes to Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The considerations for why the Government has concerns for this deal, Minister Tong has already explained.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I just wanted to reiterate one point, an important point, that Minister Tong said earlier, which is that from NE and NTUC's point of view, their objective, their intent of entering into this deal with Allianz is to strengthen Income, so that Income is in a better position to do well and to be able to meet its social obligations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Government has a different view because of the concerns that we had, as Minister Tong explained, and that is why we are coming to Parliament.

sections.label: Urgency and Insurance Act amendment
sections.summary: The speaker explained the Bill's urgency because shareholders are considering the deal, and the Insurance Act has no explicit provision for MAS to consider non-prudential factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: While I can understand the urgency of the intervention by the Government, can I ask is there not any provision within our existing legislation that allows the Minister-in-charge to reject corporate transactions on grounds of public interest, rather than to amend the Insurance Act on the basis of a Certificate of Urgency?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I have explained earlier why there is urgency in tabling this Bill – because the deal is under consideration by the shareholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Currently, there is no explicit provision in the Insurance Act for MAS to consider non-prudential-related factors in assessing such applications.
